newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Baan first half seen more than doubling.
newsitem.headline: Baan first half seen more than doubling.

text.p: Dutch computer software firm Baan will more than double its half year profit when it reports late on Wednesday, as revenue growth and margin improvement continues, analysts said on Friday.
Most forecasts ranged from $25 million to $29 million with consensus around $26 million, against $11.19 million in the first half of 1996.

The growth of the business software market, including rising sales of products which address the problems linked to the date change at the turn of the millennium, was likely to have been the main reason for Baan's improvements, said analysts.
"Their market is still strong. They will be helped by the (strong) dollar as well," said Steven Vrolijk of ING Barings.
But, said analysts, Baan is also expected to have gained from its own strategy concentrating on smaller scale companies and on sales via retailers.
"We expect strong growth in the small to medium sized area...It was an area they targetted as of late last year," said Marja Zandstra of BZW.
Margins are likely to have improved with concentration on licensing and the outsourcing of lower margin activities such as servicing.
However, Baan has set an ambitious target of 18-20 percent operating margins for this year and of above 20 percent for next.
"It achieved (a margin of) 16 percent in Q1 and it will be interesting to see if they can achieve the higher levels they need," said Pieter van Gelder of Delta Lloyd Bank.
Analysts and the trading community will also be interested to hear how soon Baan expects to introduce the next wave Baan V systems which promise to offer customers greater flexibility.
"They said it would probably be achieved in the fourth quarter. We would be interested to know if it can be any sooner," said Zandstra.

Analysts said they wished to learn of Baan's progress in targetting middle-sized companies and sales via third parties in the United States. Some added they would also want to hear if Baan has made or intends to make greater strides in developing markets such as in Asia. -- Philip Blenkinsop, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
